jobs.occupation: Specialkok i kantonesisk Siu Mei / Chinese BBQ.     Cantonese Siu Mei / Chinese BBQ Specialist Chef
jobs.description:
Specialkok – kantonesisk Siu Mei / kinesisk BBQ

Magasasa driver flere kinesiske restauranter i København. Som en del af vores videre udvikling ønsker vi at etablere og udvikle et nyt område med fokus på traditionel kantonesisk Siu Mei.

Vi søger derfor en erfaren specialkok, som har professionel erfaring specifikt med kantonesisk Siu Mei. Stillingen er ikke en almindelig kokkestilling, men kræver specialiseret erfaring med traditionelle kantonesiske stegeteknikker.

Arbejdsopgaver

• Produktion af traditionel kantonesisk Siu Mei, herunder helstegt and, Char Siu og sprødstegt svinekød
• Ansvar for processen fra forberedelse til færdigt produkt
• Sikring af ensartet kvalitet og høj standard
• Bidrage til udvikling og standardisering af vores nye Siu Mei-produktlinje
• Overholdelse af gældende krav til fødevaresikkerhed og køkkenhygiejne

Kvalifikationer

• Minimum 3 års dokumenterbar professionel erfaring med kantonesisk Siu Mei / kinesisk BBQ
• Erfaring med selvstændig produktion af helstegt and, Char Siu og sprødstegt svinekød
• Kendskab til traditionelle kantonesiske tilberedningsmetoder og professionelt Siu Mei-udstyr
• Selvstændig, kvalitetsbevidst og ansvarlig

Vi tilbyder en mulighed for at blive en del af Magasasas næste udviklingsfase og være med til at opbygge vores nye kantonesiske Siu Mei-koncept.

Send CV og en kort beskrivelse af din relevante erfaring til mail: job@magasasa.dk

Cantonese Siu Mei / Chinese BBQ Specialist Chef

Magasasa operates several Chinese restaurants in Copenhagen. As part of our next stage of development, we are establishing a new specialised area focusing on traditional Cantonese Siu Mei.

We are looking for an experienced specialist chef with professional experience specifically in Cantonese Siu Mei. This is not a general chef position and requires specialised knowledge of traditional Cantonese roasting techniques.

Responsibilities

• Production of traditional Cantonese Siu Mei, including whole roast duck, Char Siu and crispy roast pork
• Managing the production process from preparation to finished product
• Maintaining consistent quality and high production standards
• Contributing to the development and standardisation of our new Siu Mei product line
• Maintaining professional food safety and kitchen hygiene standards

Qualifications

• Minimum 3 years of documented professional experience in Cantonese Siu Mei / Chinese BBQ
• Experience independently producing whole roast duck, Char Siu and crispy roast pork
• Knowledge of traditional Cantonese preparation techniques and professional Siu Mei equipment
• Ability to work independently with a strong focus on quality and consistency

We offer an opportunity to take part in Magasasa’s next stage of development and help establish our new Cantonese Siu Mei concept.

Please send your CV and a short description of your relevant professional experience to mail: job@magasasa.dk

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Computational Mass Spectrometry Imaging and Spatial Metabolomics
jobs.description:
PhD Position in Computational Mass Spectrometry Imaging and Spatial Metabolomics
Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at the Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Roskilde Campus, Denmark, within the Environmental Science and Toxicology department. The position is available from February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Title
PhD Position in Computational Mass Spectrometry Imaging and Spatial Metabolomics

Research area and project description
Spatial metabolomics enables the study of biochemical processes and human–environment interactions at micrometer to cellular resolution (single cell metabolomics). Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) is increasingly used to investigate how environmental stressors and micropollutants affect biological systems across space and time. However, data processing, image segmentation, multimodal image registration, reproducible computational workflows and biological interpretation remain major challenges.

This project will develop computational methods and open-source tools for processing, analyzing and interpreting MSI and spatial metabolomics data. The methods will be applied to microbial communities, environmental samples and tissues to uncover spatially resolved biotransformation processes and metabolic responses to environmental stressors.

The successful candidate will work at the interface of computational science, biochemistry, microbiology and analytical chemistry. The project will combine computational method development with experimental spatial metabolomics including signal preprocessing, machine learning, spatial statistics, image registration and interactive software development. The PhD student will join an interdisciplinary team of chemists, microbiologists, biologists and computational scientists and contribute to both methodological development and biological applications.

The position includes:
• Developing batch-processing workflows for MSI and metabolomics data, including normalization, quantification and feature alignment.
• Developing spatial segmentation methods, including uncertainty-aware and spatially regularized clustering.
• Collaborating with experimental scientists, mass spectrometrists and biologists to validate methods against experimental and biological datasets. Ensure reliable implementation of automated quality control, testing, documentation and reproducibility reporting.
• Communicating computational results clearly to interdisciplinary and non-computational re-searchers. Processing and analyzing imaging datasets and presenting results at internal and international scientific meetings.
• Publishing methodological and application studies and releasing well-documented open-source software.
• Close supervision and collaboration with dedicated researchers and senior investigators.
Project description
For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences
We are seeking highly motivated candidates with a strong interest in interdisciplinary research. Applicants should hold a master’s degree (or equivalent) in computer science, bioinformatics/ cheminformatics, AI/ML, data science, chemistry, computational biology, chemometrics, analytical chemistry or a related discipline.

Essential qualifications:
• Solid background in computational chemistry, image processing, omics data analysis and/or mass spectrometry
• Strong interest in spatial metabolomics and its applicationsDesirable qualifications:
• Experience with mass spectrometry, microscopy, microbial systems, or analytical chemistry
• Ability to work independently as well as in collaborative, interdisciplinary teams
Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Environmental Science, Roskilde Campus, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
 
• Prasad Phapale, prasad.phapale@envs.au.dk (main supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk
How to apply:
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 30 November 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 01 February 2027.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants. All interested candidates are encouraged to apply, regardless of their personal background. Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with applicable collective agreement.

jobs.occupation: Optical Design Engineers for our High Power Beam Combining team
jobs.description:
Optical Design Engineers for our High Power Beam Combining team

Location: Farum, Denmark | Level: PhD / Postdoc / Experienced Engineer

The Mission: Build the Next Generation of SBC Systems

At Ibsen Photonics, we are developing Spectral Beam Combining (SBC) modules for high-power laser architectures. We are looking for creative, hands-on Optical Design Engineers to take full ownership of designing, building, and optimising our SBC platform.

This role bridges the gap between theoretical physics and industrial reality. You won’t just design on a screen; you will spend significant time in the lab, iterating rapidly from proof-of-concept to robust, production-ready, scalable systems.

Key responsibilities:

• Design & Assemble: Develop compact, efficient SBC modules using Ibsen’s world-class transmission gratings, while considering optical beam paths, thermal effects and mechanical constraints.

• System Optimisation: Drive performance by refining optical alignment, mechanical stability, and complex thermal management for high-power loads in a reiterative process: design – experiment – optimise.

• Characterisation: Use advanced diagnostics to maintain beam quality (low M²) during power scaling, including wavefront sensing and spectral analysis.

• Full Lifecycle Ownership: Source optical/mechanical components and manage the transition from experimental prototypes to scalable, volume-ready designs.

• Global Collaboration: Work closely with an internal team and international partners, including potential overseas visits for joint prototyping and testing.

What you bring

You are a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a “build-test-learn” environment. Ideally, you possess:

• Education: A PhD or Postdoc in Optics, Photonics, Laser Physics, or a related field.

• Expertise:

• Hands on experience with (high-power) fibre and free-space optical systems, precise alignment, and experimental troubleshooting.

• Understanding of (and ideally experience with) SBC and CBC beam combining techniques.

• Beam quality measurement and analysis.

• Mechanical design of low-tolerance devices

• Technical Knowledge: Deep understanding of Gaussian optics, beam propagation, and high-power laser effects (thermal lensing, runaway-effects, mitigation strategies).

• Software Skills: Proficiency in optical simulation tools (e.g., Zemax) and familiarity with mechanical CAD.

• Mindset: Independent enough to drive a project and work on your own, but collaborative enough to thrive in a flat-hierarchy, cross-functional team, sharing insights and discussing projects/next steps. The role is highly experimental and hands-on, requiring independence and a strong drive to make systems work in practice, not just on paper.

• Security Clearance: You are a European citizen with no family ties to Russia or Russian allied territories, and you have a clean criminal record.

Why join Ibsen Photonics?

• High Impact: Your designs will directly shape the future of high-brightness laser systems for manufacturing, defence, telecommunications, and science.

• Freedom to Innovate: We value experimental drive—if you have a better way to align or stabilise a system, we want to see it.

• Danish Engineering Culture: Enjoy a supportive environment with fast decision-making, real ownership, and a healthy work-life balance.

Application

We are looking to recruit as soon as possible but will keep the positions open until we have found the right candidates. If you want more information about the positions, please call Henrik Skov Andersen on +45 4434 7023 or email [henrik.s.andersen @ibsen.com](

jobs.occupation: Specialistläkare/överläkare inom kardiologi till Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital i Slagelse, Danmark
jobs.description:
Om du är på jakt för nya utmaningar på jobbet och funderar på att jobba i Danmark är kardiologen på Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital i Slagelse ett självklart val.

Här kan du vara med och påverka framtidens hjärtmedicin och samtidigt få möjlighet att utveckla och leda ditt eget specialområde.

På hjärtmedicinska avdelningen (Medicin 2) kommer du som specialistläkare att spela en central roll för den kliniska verksamheten och yrkesområdets utveckling. Du kommer att arbeta i nära samarbete med avdelningens övriga specialistläkare, chefer och andra professioner för att skapa smidiga och sammanhängande patientförlopp.

Yrkesmässiga utmaningar och ett flexibelt arbetsliv

Som specialistläkare hos oss får du inte bara en tjänst. Du får möjlighet att styra inriktningen inom ett eller flera specialområden, om du har ambitionen och intresset för det.

Du får

• möjlighet att ta ansvar för och utveckla ett helt eget specialområde inom exempelvis ischemi, arytmi, hjärtklaffssjukdomar eller bilddiagnostik i form av ekokardiografi, hjärt-CT och hjärt-MR

• möjlighet att delta i forskningen vid avdelningen

• möjlighet att ingå i en högspecialiserad miljö med engagerade kollegor

• ett nära samarbete med övriga professioner och en hög grad av kollegialt utbyte.

Dessutom kan vi anpassa tjänsten så att den passar dina behov. På Medicin 2 lägger vi stor vikt vid att skapa balans mellan arbete och fritid, och vi prioriterar stort inflytande och ansvar.

Om dig

Vi tror att du

• är specialistläkare i kardiologi, eller är på väg att bli det

• fokuserar på att utveckla vårdkvaliteten och förbättra patientförloppet

• trivs i en miljö där man både för ett nära samarbete och arbetar självständigt

• bidrar till en aktiv och god arbetsmiljö

• har ett intresse för kvalitet, utbildning och eventuellt forskning

• kommunicerar öppet och konstruktivt.

Om oss

Vår avdelning bedriver verksamhet i två olika lokaler i Næstved respektive Slagelse, som ligger 30 km från varandra.

I Slagelse består avdelningen av två vårdavdelningar med 24 respektive 20 sängplatser. Därutöver har vi en hjärtmottagning samt det vårdmässiga ansvaret för en hormonmottagning.

I Næstved består avdelningen av ett trombos- och koagulationscentrum, en hjärtmottagning samt det vårdmässiga ansvaret för en hormonmottagning. Utöver detta rymmer lokalerna även ett diagnostiskt centrum.

Vi är för närvarande 12 specialistläkare inom kardiologi samt specialistläkare inom avdelningens övriga specialistfunktioner.

Vi ansvarar för undervisningen av medicinstudenter från Köpenhamns universitet.

Därför ska du välja Midt- och Vestsjællands Hospital

På Midt- och Vestsjællands Hospital fokuserar vi på yrkeskompetens, samarbete mellan professioner, kvalitet, utbildning och forskning.

Specialister spelar en central roll både för den kliniska verksamheten och för den ämnesspecifika utvecklingen, och du blir en del av en miljö med hög grad av specialisering, tydliga ambitioner och goda möjligheter att påverka utvecklingen inom ditt specialistområde.

Vi erbjuder en arbetsplats där fokus ligger på vårdkvalitet, kontinuitet i patientförloppet och förutsättningar som främjar såväl kliniskt arbete som utbildning och forskning.

Din huvudsakliga arbetsplats kommer att vara i Slagelse som har goda transportförbindelser med bland annat Odense, Köpenhamn och övriga Själland.

Är du redo för nästa steg?

Vill du vara med och utveckla kardiologin på Midt- og Vestsjælland? Då ser vi gärna att du hör av dig.

Mer information

Om du vill ha mer information om tjänsten är du välkommen att kontakta tillförordnad chefsläkare Roman Sykulski på tel. +45 56 51 41 34 eller chefsjuksköterska Camilla Vest på tel. +45 93 56 84 89.

Villkor, lön och anställning

Du kommer att ingå i ett jourteam med bakjoursansvar från ditt eget hem i egenskap av överläkare och ha jour utanför arbetsplatsen i egenskap av specialistläkare.

Vi har omfattande erfarenhet av att hitta flexibla lösningar som möjliggör ett hållbart arbetsliv, så kontakta oss gärna för ett förutsättningslöst samtal om vilka möjligheter som finns.

Den professionella bedömningen av sökanden kommer att baseras på sökandens uppgifter om sina egna kompetenser i förhållande till de sju läkartjänsterna. Om du söker en tjänst som överläkare kommer en professionell bedömning att genomföras som kommer att vara avgörande för din kvalifikation som överläkare.

Anställningen sker enligt avtalet mellan Danske Regioner och YL/Overlægeforeningen, beroende på vilken tjänst som söks, och är villkorad med att det finns en tillfredsställande børneattest (utdrag ur belastningsregistret som visar om en person dömts för sexualbrott mot barn under 15 år).

Vi önskar tillsätta tjänsten senast eller enligt överenskommelse.

Hjälp med flytt och undervisning i danska

Om du vill flytta till Danmark i samband med anställningen erbjuder vi kostnadsfri, professionell hjälp med flytt och bosättning nära sjukhuset eller eventuellt i Köpenhamn. Du får hjälp med allt från att hitta boende till registrering och eventuella medföljande familjemedlemmar.

En viktig del av arbetet som specialistläkare är kommunikationen mellan läkare och patient. För patientsäkerhetens skull kräver därför Region Sjælland att våra specialistläkare ska ha kunskaper i danska språket på en tillfredsställande nivå. Vi tillhandahåller därför en språklärare för privatundervisning så att du så snabbt som möjligt kan kommunicera med dina patienter på en nivå där ni förstår varandra.

Det innebär att vi förväntar oss att du är inställd på att lägga tid på att lära dig danska, både i tal och skrift.

Se mer om vad vi erbjuder i form av hjälp här

Rekryteringsprocessen

När vi har mottagit din ansökan kommer vi att bedöma om dina kvalifikationer matchar det vi söker, och du kommer initialt att bjudas in till en intervju via Teams. Om båda parter är intresserade av att fortsätta dialogen kommer du att bjudas in till ett rekryteringssamtal på sjukhuset, där du får träffa avdelningens ledning och personal samt vår HR- och språkkonsult.

Ansökningstid

Vi kommer att granska ansökningarna till tjänsten löpande, så vänta inte för länge med att ansöka.

Verksamhetsområde

Den 1 januari 2027 slås Region Själland och Region Hovedstaden samman och bildar Region Østdanmark till följd av sjukvårdsreformen. Ditt verksamhetsområde kommer att vara Region Østdanmark, inklusive alla tillhörande organisatoriska enheter.

Läs mer om vad verksamhetsområdet innebär på Region Østdanmarks webbplats.

Om Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital

På Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital arbetar vi varje dag för att främja ett hälsosamt liv genom förebyggande åtgärder och behandling inom ramen för en samordnad hälso- och sjukvårdsinsats. Som sjukhus förenar vi psykiatri och somatik. Vårt mål är att patienter och medborgare ska få bra och trygg vård av hög kvalitet.

Som medarbetare blir du en del av ett innovativt, kompetent och organisatoriskt stabilt sjukhus där vi gör skillnad för de människor som behöver oss. Lärande och utveckling är en del av vardagen och sker i professionella sammanhang med ett gemensamt ansvar. Det sker även mellan olika avdelningar.

Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital betjänar ett upptagningsområde med cirka 230 000 invånare. Vi har 766 vårdplatser och cirka 5 000 anställda fördelade på 20 avdelningar, däribland 16 somatiska och psykiatriska avdelningar.

Vi erbjuder en gedigen forskningsmiljö med 13 professorer och en stark yrkesmässig utbildningsmiljö, där vi varje år välkomnar cirka 2 700 studenter, elever och läkare som deltar i vidareutbildning.

Ansættelsesområde

Region Sjælland og Region Hovedstaden bliver den 1. januar 2027 til Region Østdanmark som følge af sundhedsreformen. Dit ansættelsesområde vil være Region Østdanmark med alle tilhørende organisatoriske enheder.

Læs mere om betydningen af ansættelsesområdet på Region Østdanmarks hjemmeside.

Startløn for overenskomstansatte

Regionen er forpligtet til at oplyse dig om startlønnen for stillingen. Du får oplyst grundløn, centralt fastsatte tillæg og pension i den relevante overenskomst. Udover startlønnen, kan lønnen indeholde eventuelt forhandlede tillæg afhængigt af stillingen, dine erfaringer og kvalifikationer.

Se startlønnen på regionens hjemmeside

Om Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital

På Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital arbejder vi hver dag for at fremme det sunde liv ved at forebygge og behandle i en sammenhængende sundhedsindsats. Som hospital forener vi psykiatri og somatik. Vores mål er, at patienter og borgere oplever gode og trygge forløb af høj kvalitet.

Som medarbejder bliver du en del af et nytænkende, fagligt og organisatorisk robust hospital, hvor vi gør en forskel for de mennesker, der har brug for os. Læring og udvikling er en del af hverdagen og sker i fagligt forpligtende fællesskaber. Også på tværs af afdelinger.

Midt- og Vestsjællands Hospital dækker et opland på ca. 230.000 borgere. Vi har 766 sengepladser og er omkring 5.000 ansatte fordelt på 20 afdelinger, herunder 16 somatiske og psykiatriske specialer.

Vi tilbyder et solidt forskningsmiljø med 13 professorer og et stærkt fagligt uddannelsesmiljø, hvor vi hvert år byder cirka 2.700 studerende, elever og læger i videreuddannelsesforløb velkommen.

jobs.occupation: Customer Manager
jobs.description:
**About Us

nShift is the leading global provider of cloud delivery management solutions (SaaS), we enable the frictionless shipment and return of almost one billion shipments across 190 countries each year. We are headquartered in London and Oslo and have over 460 employees across offices in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, the United Kingdom, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Romania.

Our software is used by many of the world leading e-commerce, retail, manufacturing, and 3PL shippers due to us having over 1000 carriers integrated into our platform, nearly 3 times more than our competitors!

If you buy goods online, there is a strong chance that nShift has powered that delivery, so come and join us as we shape the future of shipping, one frictionless journey at a time.

**Purpose of role

**As a Customer Manager, you'll own the long-term success and commercial growth of a portfolio of mid- & enterprise sized customers across your home market in Denmark. jobs.occupation: Fully funded PhD position in Korean Studies at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies
jobs.description:
The Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies in the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a full-time three-year PhD scholarship, with an expected starting date of 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The PhD project will be part of the research project Sensing Korea: Reframing Korean Studies in the Nordic Countries, funded by the Academy of Korean Studies. Sensing Korea aims to develop sensory and narrative approaches to Korean Studies in order to explore the diversity of Korean experiences beyond essentializing representations.

  The PhD scholarship is funded through the Core University Program for Korean Studies of the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Korea and the Korean Studies Promotion Service at the Academy of Korean Studies (AKS-2026-OLU-2250001). Sensing Korea is led by Barbara Wall and hosted by Korean Studies at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, University of Copenhagen. The project runs for five years, from June 2026 to May 2031.

  The PhD candidate will be supervised by project leader Barbara Wall and will work closely with a project team comprising scholars based at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies as well as researchers from Korean Studies programs at other Nordic universities. The candidate is also expected to have an interest in communicating academic knowledge about Korea to a broader public.

  About the department
 The project is based at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, which is part of the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen. The department has approximately 800 students and 150 employees. At the department, we research and teach in language, culture, religion and society, primarily with a focus on regions outside Western Europe and the USA. The work is rooted in language-based area studies and cross-cultural perspectives that provide insight into global contexts and cultural complexity.

  Introduction to the PhD programme
 PhD studies consist of research programmes that qualify students for independent and wide-ranging research, development and teaching at international level. The main emphasis is on PhD students organising and conducting their own research project (under supervision). The programme culminates in the submission of a PhD thesis, which the student must defend in public. The programme is prescribed to 180 ECTS points, corresponding to three years of full-time study. The PhD will have to teach and carry out other tasks at the department as part of the PhD position corresponding to 840 working hours (6 months).

  A PhD opens up a range of career opportunities in academia and elsewhere. As well as writing a thesis, PhD students work in active research environments in Denmark and abroad. They contribute to the academic environment, take research training courses and convey the results of their research in teaching, at academic conferences and to the general public. 

  Qualification requirements
 Applicants must have qualifications corresponding to a master’s degree in Korean Studies or a related field in the humanities. Particularly relevant disciplinary backgrounds and research interests include Literary Studies and Sensory Studies, as well as Musicology, Media Studies, Religious Studies, Cultural Studies, History, Art History/Visual Culture, Performance Studies, and East Asian Studies. If you have completed your education in Denmark, you must have a master’s degree covered by the collective agreement for academics in the state sector.

  The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Korean Studies or a related humanities discipline, with research interests in Literary Studies and/or Sensory Studies, or in another relevant field with a clear connection to sensory and narrative approaches to Korea. Excellent proficiency in Korean and English is essential. Proficiency in a Scandinavian language and/or Literary Sinitic (Hanmun) is considered an advantage.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, you must either have a master’s degree equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (two years) or as minimum a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree (three years) and be assessed as having professional qualifications at master's level.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, we will obtain an assessment of your education from the Danish Research Agency. Applicants must possess skills in written and spoken academic English at a high level. Additional language skills and knowledge of related regions is an advantage. If deemed necessary, the department may request that applicants document their English or other language skills.

  Application
 All applications must be submitted online, in PDF or Microsoft Word format, via the link “Apply for the position” at the bottom of the page. 

  The application must include: 

  Personal statement (max. one page)
 In their personal statements, applicants are encouraged to: 

   	
• outline how the PhD project relates to other research activities at the department, particularly the Sensing Korea project.  	
• describe as clearly as possible their competencies and personal qualifications relevant to the PhD programme and the Sensing Korea project.   CV
 Applications must be accompanied by a CV (max.one page) and a list of publications, where relevant. 

  Documentation (diplomas and transcripts) 
 Applicants must upload the following:

   	
• A copy of their Master’s degree diploma or similar (if this is not available by the application deadline, applicants must document pre-approval of their Master’s thesis) 	
• A copy of their Master’s degree transcript 	
• A copy of their Bachelor’s degree diploma 	
• A copy of their Bachelor’s degree transcript.   Applicants with a degree from a university where the working language is not English or one of the Scandinavian languages must submit a translation of their Master’s diploma and/or diploma transcripts approved by the issuing university of by another local authority. These documents must be translated into English, Danish, Norwegian or Swedish. An official description of the grading scale (and a diploma supplement where relevant) must also be attached. 

  Chinese applicants must attach a China Credentials Verification (CHSI) certificate. Read more about CHSI here: https://www.chsi.com.cn/xlcx/en/index.jsp.

  Project description 
 Applications must include a preliminary project description covering the problem formulation, overall objectives, methodology, design and timetable (max. five pages/12,000 characters, incl. spaces, excl. bibliography). The project description should also give a preliminary indication of what research literature the candidate would expect to engage with. 
 
 On the website of the PhD School, you can find more information about the attachments your need to include with your application:PhD at the Faculty of Humanities – University of Copenhagen / https://phd.humanities.ku.dk/how-to-obtain-a-phd-scholarship/admission-requirements/ .

  Please do not upload or submit recommendations, publications, theses, etc. 

  Assessment criteria
 The following criteria are applied when assessing PhD applications:

   	
• The quality, originality and feasibility of the PhD project and its relevance to the Sensing Korea project 	
• Research qualifications, as reflected in the attached CV and project description  	
• Competencies and knowledge of relevant fields of academic research 	
• Level (grades obtained) of Bachelor and Master’s studies.    Please note that only one position is available and competition is intense. 

  The recruitment process 
 After the deadline for applications, the Head of Department considers advice from the Appointment Committee and then selects applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether or not they have been shortlisted. After this, the Head of Department sets up an expert Assessment Committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Individual applicants will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment of their application before the appointment is announced.

  Enrolment 
 It is a prerequisite for employment that successful applicants enrol at the PhD School of the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen. 
 For further information about the structure of the PhD programme, please refer to: Structure of the PhD programme – University of Copenhagen
 For further information about the guidelines for PhD studies at UCPH, please refer to: https://phd.ku.dk/english/

  Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC).
 The salary range starts at approximately DKK 30,200 (EUR 4.040) + an 18.07 % pension contribution. According to the agreement, the PhD student is required to carry out tasks at the relevant department to an extent corresponding to 840 working hours (6 months). These tasks are primarily expected to consist of teaching in the department’s study programmes.

  You can read more about employment as a PhD Fellow here: Employment as a PhD student – University of Copenhagen.

  International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk).

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in research, please visit: HR Excellence in Research – University of Copenhagen.

  For further information about the application procedure, please refer to the University of Copenhagen website: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Contact Information
 Information about the recruitment process is available from HR South at: hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2541/26-2H.

  If you have any questions about the academic content of the PhD programme, please e-mail the PhD coordinator at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, Simon Stjernholm, stjernholm@hum.ku.dk.
 If you have questions related to the Sensing Korea project, please email PI Barbara Wall, barbara.wall@hum.ku.dk
 
 The deadline for applications is 1 November 2026 at 23:59 (CET).
 Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.

jobs.occupation: Process Specialist for E-beam and UV Lithography - DTU Nanolab
jobs.description:
If you are an experienced engineer/physicist within e-beam and UV lithography, we can offer you an exciting workplace at the Technical University of Denmark. 

The cleanroom facility DTU Nanolab is looking for a process specialist for the lithography team. DTU Nanolab is one of the largest open access facilities in Europe. We enable top-down micro- and nanofabrication through a broad spectrum of advanced processing and measurement equipment supporting research, education and small-scale production activities in the fields of quantum technology, photonics, MEMS, microfluidics, biochemistry and polymer processing.

The job
As our new Process Specialist, you will work with e-beam and UV lithography. Your main responsibilities will include:

• Process development and troubleshooting within lithography processes and equipment.
• Daily maintenance of our JEOL JBX-9500FSZ and Raith e-LINE Plus e-beam lithography systems.
• Process development and QC work on these e-beam lithography systems.
• Training users in the equipment and in process development related to e-beam lithography.
• Training users on other equipment used for UV lithography, such as automatic and manual spin coaters, mask and maskless aligners, and automatic and manual developers.
You will work closely with other process specialists and technicians in the lithography team, as well as with researchers, students and engineers from DTU and commercial companies. A large part of your working day will be spent in ISO 4 and 5 cleanrooms, where you will wear a full cleanroom suit.

You must have a M.Sc. or Ph.D. degree within either engineering or physics within a relevant field (micro/nanofabrication, experimental physics or similar) and have profound knowledge and experimental skills within the area of UV and e-beam lithography. 

Our expectations of you
You must have a Master of Science degree or, preferably, a PhD within a relevant field, such as micro/nanofabrication, physics or a similar field. Furthermore, we expect you to possess several of the following skills and qualifications:

• Hands-on experience with e-beam lithography systems.
• Profound knowledge of e-beam lithography processes.
• Hands-on experience with UV lithography.
• A deep understanding of the underlying physical and chemical processes in lithography.
• Hands-on experience working in a cleanroom environment.
• A broad understanding of micro- and nanoprocessing. 
• You have an eye for detail and work meticulously.
• You work well in teams with people from different backgrounds.
• You are service-minded.
• You are self-driven and able to plan your own working day.
• You communicate well in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Danish is an advantage.
What we offer in return
We offer an interesting and challenging job in an international work environment. You will be working with state-of-the-art semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) is a leading technical university in northern Europe and benchmarks with the best universities in the world. We place emphasis on a high level of professionalism among our staff, so skills development is an integral part of our organization. We offer a great flexibility in the position. Please note that this is not a research position, but a technical position, with a main focus to facilitate academic and industrial users within the field of e-beam and UV lithography.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Academic Officer, Senior Officer, Senior Executive Officer. 

In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The position is a full-time position, preferably starting 1 December 2026 or according to mutual agreement. 

The workplace is DTU Lyngby Campus.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than Sunday, 25 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Karen Birkelund, Head of Lithography and Wet Chemistry kabi@dtu.dk or phone +45 2179 9118.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Nanolab is a common infrastructure and research facility located at and fully owned by the Technical University of Denmark, DTU. The core facilities consist of a large cleanroom and a state-of-the-art electron microscopy. The research activities carried out at DTU Nanolab span from nano- and microfabrication with silicon-based materials, carbon and polymers to the highly sophisticated analysis of nanoscale materials down to atomic resolution. Since 2018, DTU Nanolab has extended to provide expertise in soft matter from small molecule complexes to biological cells.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Want to help rethink the foundation of the internet? Become a PhD student at DTU Electro
jobs.description:
Want to help rethink the foundation of the internet? Become a PhD student at DTU Electro – it only takes 20 minutes!

The internet is growing at an explosive pace - and so is its energy consumption. Yet light is still the most energy-efficient way to transmit information.
Today, data is sent around the globe as billions of light pulses every second, generated by millions of individual lasers.

We have shown that many of these lasers can be replaced by a single optical light source that emits a full rainbow spectrum of colours - and that each colour can act as its own “mini-laser”. In other words: one light source can do the job of many, making communication systems far more energy-efficient.

This is exactly the technology we are developing. And as a PhD student, you will play a key role in turning this concept into reality.

What will you be working on?
You will join an international research environment developing new ways of transmitting data - more energy-efficiently, more scalably, and with fewer active components.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Working on a project that combines photonics, modelling, chip design and hands-on experiments - in a field that is advancing rapidly.
• Contributing both independently and as part of a close-knit team where we support each other, share ideas, and lift the projects together.
• Being an active part of the group’s scientific and social community, where humour, curiosity, and good collaboration are part of everyday life.
• Collaborating with researchers, industry partners, and fellow PhD students in a team of around eight people.
• Participating in international research environments, including a planned 3–6 month research stay abroad.
How your time is typically divided:

• 2/3 research – your project, your models, your experiments.
• 1/6 teaching – e.g., exercises, supervision, or course assistance.
• 1/6 other activities – conferences, courses, group collaboration, social networks, and building strong collegial relations
The technical corner
If you already know exactly what “optical modulators operating at low SNR in spatially data-distributed links” means, you’re going to enjoy this.

If you don’t - even better, because that is exactly what you will learn here.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level, equivalent to a two-year master's degree, before starting the project. It may be within physics, mathematics, electrical engineering, optical communications, fibre optics, coding, or integrated photonics/nanofabrication - but whatever your background, you don’t need to know the field in depth yet. You will learn everything you need during the project.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see the Rules for the PhD proramme at DTU.

The core of your PhD project is to exploit optical frequency combs - light sources that emit a full spectrum of colours at once - and design the components that can modulate each colour’s data signal as energy-efficiently as possible.

Here are some of the concrete technical tasks you will work on:

• Design and modelling
• Learning to use chip-design software to develop optical data modulators that are:
 – energy-efficient
 – as simple as possible
 – stand-alone or co-integrated with other components
 – capable of operating at low signal-to-noise ratios (low SNR)
 – flexible in terms of modulation formats and coding
• Experiments and characterisation
• Testing and characterising your modulators in real communication setups, such as:
 – space-division multiplexed (SDM) fibre transmission systems
 – data-centre scenarios
 – unrepeatered data-distributed links
• Modulation formats
• Discovering which modulation formats actually work best when transmitting data over… yes… a rainbow of optical colours.
• Experimenting with how to achieve maximum data capacity with minimum energy.
And don’t worry: You are not expected to understand all of this yet - but if this sounds exciting, you’re exactly the kind of candidate we’re looking for.

What do we offer?
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

At DTU Electro, you get access to world-class laboratories - but also something equally important: a workplace that genuinely cares about people. 

You’ll have close supervision and mentoring from senior researchers, and a group that works together rather than in silos.

We offer:

• An open, helpful, and humorous research environment where you can ask about anything - scientific or practical.
• A culture built on respect, good manners, and a strong desire to collaborate.
• Realistic expectations, clear support, and solid scientific supervision.
• A workplace where you can conduct serious research and still enjoy yourself.
• Colleagues who help you build a strong research career - both during and after your PhD.
• DTU supports you before, during, and after parental leave, ensuring a smooth return so your research can continue to grow. As a public-sector employee in Denmark, you are entitled to paid parental leave under Danish legislation and collective agreements, providing up to 48 weeks of benefits after childbirth. The High-Speed Optical Communications group also offers extra support for young researchers, including help with maintaining research progress and preparing potential grant applications.
Apply without CV and cover letter - it only takes 20 minutes!
We use Caseflow for this recruitment, ensuring a fair and structured process that focuses only on your competences and motivation - nothing else.

That means you don’t have to submit a traditional CV or application. Instead, you simply answer a few questions about the job - and you’re already closer to an interview!

Click here to get started. (This is the only valid way to apply. Applications submitted through the DTU “Apply now” button cannot be accepted.) 

When you click, you’ll be asked to enter your email, and then a code will be sent to you.

Practical information

Salary and terms of employment
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

• Employment: Full-time (3-year PhD position).
• Start date: 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible.
• Deadline: 26 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time).
Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

Please note that applications must be submitted through Caseflow using the link above. Do NOT use the “Ansøg nu” button below, as applications submitted through that button will not be included in the assessment. 

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

More info & questions?
If you have questions, you are welcome to contact Professor Leif Katsuo Oxenløwe at +45 2635 3928 or lkox@fotonik.dtu.dk.

For questions about the recruitment process, feel free to contact Chandra Schilling at +45 4525 5177 or cschi@dtu.dk.

You are also very welcome to drop by for a chat - we’re always happy to offer you a cup of coffee.

For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

About DTU Electro
DTU Electro is one of the world’s largest research environments in photonics and electronics, with around 320 employees. We conduct research in everything from quantum photonics, nano-optics, and optical sensors to high-speed optical communications, robotics, and high-power electronics.

You will join the High-Speed Optical Communications Group (HSOC) - an international, welcoming, and collaborative team where high scientific ambition goes hand in hand with helpfulness, humour, and academic kindness. Researchers and PhD students work closely together to develop the next generation of energy-efficient and sustainable communication technologies - from optical frequency combs and new modulator designs to communication links that operate at low signal-to-noise ratios.

The group consists of around eight people and is part of a larger international network of academic and industrial partners. You will have access to advanced laboratories, state-of-the-art equipment, and colleagues who share knowledge generously, offer support, and help you move forward when something (inevitably) becomes challenging in the research process.

DTU has more than 13,500 students and 6,000 employees and is founded on a mission to develop technology for the benefit of humanity. Here, you will find academic freedom, strong communities, and the opportunity to shape your research career in a globally recognised environment.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

DTU’s website automatically shows an “Apply now” button, but this button does not apply to this position. To make sure your application is received, please use this Caseflow link to proceed (read more about the application process above).

jobs.occupation: Regulatory Business Development Lead
jobs.description:
Role Description

Join us in creating a future legacy in medical dermatology

At LEO Pharma, we are global leaders in medical dermatology. We have 115 years’ experience in bringing innovation to healthcare. And we are eager to do much more. Each year, close to 100 million people have a better day because of our medicines**.

In Global Regulatory Affairs we share a “challenge accepted” mindset and are guided by our winning behaviours of simplification, collaboration, and accountability, to achieve our goals.

Your role

As a Regulatory Business Development Lead, you will support the identification, evaluation, and progression of external innovation opportunities, ensuring robust regulatory assessments, clear value-creation perspectives, and efficient use of internal expertise to support LEO Pharma’s business development goals.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Providing expert regulatory input into portfolio and pipeline strategy, evaluation, and acceleration.

• Leading the planning and execution of regulatory due diligence activities across internal and external assets.

• Conducting comprehensive global regulatory assessments covering clinical, nonclinical, CMC, and regional requirements.

• Identifying regulatory risks, gaps, and opportunities, and developing mitigation strategies to maximise the probability of technical and regulatory success.

• Driving efficient, structured due diligence processes to optimise resource use across the portfolio.

• Delivering clear regulatory risk-benefit assessments and actionable recommendations to governance bodies.

• Partnering with Search & Evaluation and Business Development teams to embed regulatory insights into deal strategy and valuation.

• Engaging with external partners and Health Authorities.

• Contributing to the development of best practices for regulatory involvement in business development and asset evaluation.

Your qualifications

To succeed in this role, we imagine that you have the following qualifications:

• Advanced degree in a scientific field (PharmD, PhD, MD, MSc).

• 10 years of global regulatory experience in the pharmaceutical or biotech industries.

• Proven track record in driving business development regulatory excellence within a search and evaluation development model.

• Demonstrated expertise in due diligence activities, regulatory risk assessment, and pipeline-building initiatives.

• In-depth knowledge of global regulatory systems and pathways.

• Experience collaborating with external partners, Health Authorities, and cross-functional teams.

• Strategic and operational mindset with the ability to navigate fast-paced environments and balance multiple priorities and proven problem-solving capability within drug development.

Contact and Application

While this position is based in our HQ in Denmark, we are also open to a hybrid work setup across Europe, enabling you to contribute from your location while fostering close collaboration with the global team.

Your application

If this exciting opportunity aligns with your expertise, we’d love to hear from you!

You do not need to upload a cover letter, but feel free to include a few sentences in your CV about why this position excites you. Please refrain from adding a photo to your CV.

Beyond the skin

Join LEO Pharma, a global leader in medical dermatology, as we go beyond the skin to make a lasting impact.  Our innovative approach sets us apart. We are dedicated to leaving a legacy that positively impacts patients, colleagues, and our planet.

At LEO Pharma, we believe in the power of individuals to drive change. Our flat organizational structure empowers you to make a visible impact and offers versatile roles for professional growth. We value diversity and welcome applications from all qualified candidates, recognizing that our different perspectives, backgrounds, and attitudes enable us to make the best decisions. Join our passionate team at LEO Pharma and be yourself as we work together to make a difference.

For certain positions, LEO Pharma might complete a background check conducted by a third party.

jobs.occupation: Bookkeeper
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced bookkeeper who enjoys working independently and taking full responsibility for the day-to-day finances? Do you like having the full overview and making sure everything is in order – even when things get busy? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

You know what good bookkeeping requires, and you have experience taking responsibility for the full financial function. Even when things get busy.

We develop technical solutions that make a real difference for our customers – and we need you to make sure our finances are in order, so the rest of the organisation can focus on what they do best.

What will you be doing?

You will be a key part of our team, working closely with management and external partners.

In practice, this means:

• Payroll processing and payroll administration for all employees.

• Accounts payable and accounts receivable, as well as day-to-day bookkeeping.

• Budget follow-up and reporting to management.

• Preparing the annual accounts and ensuring everything is ready for the audit on time.

Who are you?

You have at least 5 years of experience as a bookkeeper and are an experienced SAP user. You know your way around financial accounts, and you are comfortable taking responsibility for the company’s overall financial operations. You communicate clearly in Danish and English – and if you also speak German, that is a plus.

Most importantly, you take responsibility, work in a structured way and find practical solutions rather than waiting for them to appear.

What do we offer?

Based in Aalborg with limited travel. An informal culture with short decision-making processes and a strong sense of professional pride. The opportunity to shape your own responsibilities and develop your skills as part of a team of talented colleagues across different disciplines. Salary based on qualifications.

Application

If you would like to hear more about the position or have any questions, please feel free to contact COO Klaus Knudsen on +45 31 43 40 60 or at klaus.knudsen@aalborg-hcs.com

The position starts in November – preferably sooner.

Please send your application to job@aalborg-hcs.com

The application deadline is as soon as possible. We will conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and hire once we have found the right candidate.

We look forward to receiving your application.

About aalborg hc systems

At aalborg hc systems, we design and deliver thermal systems for district heating networks in the Nordics, Germany and the rest of Europe. We help utilities and municipalities electrify and transform their heat supply – without compromising on security of supply or economy. It’s a specialised discipline that only a few companies in Europe master – and we’re proud of that.

We were formerly the low temperature division of Aalborg CSP and continue from 2026 as an independent company within the German Alois Müller Group. In Aalborg we are around 25 employees – and around 1,100 across the group.

jobs.occupation: Project Manager for strategic property projects
jobs.description:
Project Manager for strategic property projects

Would you like to use your project management expertise to deliver property projects that make a difference?

Copenhagen Contractors A/S is a Danish company operating internationally. We value agility, teamwork and a flat organisational structure in which employees take initiative and adopt a hands-on approach. We are looking for a Project Manager to support the planning, management and delivery of projects across national and international markets.

Copenhagen Contractors A/S is a subsidiary of Copenhagen Group A/S. The company operates within the defense sector and delivers complex projects and turnkey solutions for major national and international clients, including the United Nations and the Danish Armed Forces.

We are currently working on several property development projects, with further projects in the pipeline. You will primarily be involved in national projects, with occasional international assignments, while being based at our headquarters in Nordhavn, Copenhagen.**

About the role**

You will become a key member of a newly established Real Estate department within a well-established company. The department will consist of approximately four colleagues: you, the Head of Real Estate, an Architect and a Project Developer.

You will work on a diverse range of projects, ranging in size from approximately 300 to 15,000 m². These include defense-related developments, offices, residential projects and water-related construction projects. We work with temporary, semi-permanent and permanent structures, although the majority of our projects involve permanent construction.

As Project Manager, you will be responsible for driving projects from initial ideas and concepts through planning, pricing, design and construction to final delivery. You will coordinate internal and external stakeholders and help ensure that projects are delivered in accordance with agreed objectives, timelines, budgets and quality requirements.

We believe in short decision-making processes. You will therefore experience a high degree of autonomy and minimal unnecessary administration. In return, we expect you to take initiative, demonstrate ownership, and have the confidence and ability to make decisions and drive projects forward.**

Your profile**

We imagine that you:

• Have +5 years of experience within project and construction management.

• Have a practical understanding of the construction process and appreciate the relationship between functionality, buildability, quality and cost.

• Are structured, pragmatic and solution-oriented and are comfortable coordinating consultants, contractors and other project stakeholders.

• Have a strong network among consultants and main contactors in the Danish market.

• Are motivated by autonomy, responsibility and the opportunity to influence projects rather than by rigid processes and traditional management structures.

• Have an entrepreneurial approach and enjoy taking initiative, making decisions and assuming responsibility for new areas.

• Are fluent in both Danish and English, in writing and in speech. English is the company’s official working language.

Could this be your next opportunity?

You can submit your application through our website, and if you would like to learn more about the role, you are always welcome to contact:

**Head of Real Estate

Lars Bramsen

**Phone: +45 2116 8959

Email: labr@cphgroup.com

jobs.occupation: Student Assistant, Netcompany Consulting
jobs.description:
Job Description

Would you like to be part of exciting and challenging projects within the IT world? Do you dream of having the opportunity to contribute to some of Denmark’s most business-critical IT solutions? Then we have the ideal student job for you.

At Netcompany, we are looking for a student who wants to take part in our innovative projects. Here, you will have the chance to influence our solutions while working alongside some of the industry’s most skilled colleagues, who will inspire you and support your learning.

Responsibilities and technologies

As a student assistant with us, you will be given responsibility from day one and become an important part of one of our teams. You will experience how your work directly contributes and creates value in the solutions we deliver to our clients. A student position with us gives you the opportunity to take on challenging tasks on equal footing with our full-time consultants.

We follow a well-established methodology from identifying client needs to implementing and rolling out solutions. You will therefore gain hands-on experience with developing IT systems from start to finish. You will primarily work on IT solutions and service-oriented architectures based on .NET and Java technologies, typically within maintenance, development and testing. The role provides the opportunity to put many of the skills gained during your studies into practice.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Developing functional and technical designs for system components.

• Programming tasks across all layers of the system.

• Configuration and development of extensions for standard platforms.

• Automation of business processes.

About you

We are looking for a student who can work approximately 16 hours per week. We are flexible during exam periods, but availability is expected in the lead-up to project deadlines and other key milestones. To succeed in this role, you:

• Are in the final year of your bachelor’s degree or have started a master’s degree in engineering, computer science, software, IT, or a similar field.

• Have some experience with object-oriented programming and familiarity with languages such as C# .NET and/or Java.

• Are highly motivated and eager to develop your skills.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

Send us your application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

jobs.occupation: Account Manager
jobs.description:
Retire the ERP

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers - automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Fuse Energy.

We're an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you're excited to modernise how companies run money, you're in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors including Balderton and Atomico and advised by industry titans, we're building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

About the Role

You'll sit at the heart of our Customer function and work with our most important customers. You’ll make sure they understand the value Light brings them and drive renewals and upsell.

Your customers are Financial Controllers, Finance Directors and CFOs at fast-growing multinational SaaS and tech companies. Senior, technical, time-poor. They expect you to keep up, to tell them straight when something won't work, and to make their team the hero.

We’re a young company, and we’re just starting to renew contracts. In parallel, we’re deploying Agentic Customer Engineers who help our customers make the most of Light. While they re-design customer workflows and deploy agents, you’ll own the stakeholders, the adoption, and the commercial in this motion. There's no set playbook yet. You'll write it, and we'll help.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Own existing customer relationships and drive adoption, renewal and upsell

• 
Ensure that Controllers, Finance Directors, and CFOs see the value Light brings

• 
Make finance the hero - help them do their best work and get recognition for it

• 
Partner two-in-a-box with Agentic Customer Engineers to help customers make the most of Light and our suite of AI agents

• 
Spot an engagement going sideways before the customer does, and fix it

• 
Feed what you learn back into the playbook the team is building

Experience & Qualifications

• 
5+ years owning customers in account management, customer success, consulting, or a commercial delivery role - with outcomes you can point to

• 
You hold your own with a CFO. You can talk multi-entity finance, ROI, and adoption without flinching, and you know when to push back

• 
You've driven adoption and expansion, not just kept accounts warm and sent QBRs

• 
You bring structure to messy, ambiguous engagements - clear plans, sharp prioritisation, and the judgement to know which details matter

• 
You've owned accounts and driven outcomes

• 
You use AI tools daily and have specific opinions on where they help and where they don't

• 
Fluent English; additional European languages a plus

• 
Bonus #1: Finance or accounting background

• 
Bonus #2: Experience in a forward-deployed, solutions-led, or professional-services model focused on renewals and upsell, ideally in the context of AI

You'll probably struggle here if

• 
You need a big support team, a mature playbook, and a manager on call to operate - this is a founding role with limited scaffolding

• 
You can't give a concrete example of telling a senior customer "no" and making it stick

• 
You love the status quo - this job is about change more than maintenance

• 
You've used ChatGPT once and weren't impressed - we go all in on AI at Light

The good stuff

In addition to being part of a great team and working in a really fun and innovative environment, we offer:

💸 A competitive salary + potential stock options

🏝 Generous package of paid annual leave + public holidays

🥳 Regular socials and company off-sites (last time was in Piemonte, next time is in Provence)

🚀 A huge opportunity for career growth as you'll help shape a market-defining motion

The famous last words

Working at Light means you're embarking on an exciting journey to reshape the future of multinational financial operations. Our cheat-code is that we've built something like this before - and are now doing it again, only better. Our goal is to make global finance effortless and empower companies to make informed decisions.

Join the rocket ship while it's taking off 🚀

Light is the new way to run multinational finances for modern technology companies. Run AR, AP, expenses, bookkeeping, and financial reporting automatically across all your entities — without the chaos of multiple systems. Crafted and built by the designers and engineers behind world-class companies like Spotify, X, AWS, Klarna, Google and Shopify, we empower multinational finances with a joyful user experience like no other.
